newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National up as mortgage activity rises.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National up as mortgage activity rises.

text.p: Shares in retail banking group Abbey National Plc rose on Wednesday following signs that mortgage activity in Britain is buoyant and on positive comments from brokers, traders said.
Shares in Britain's second largest home loan lender rose 11p to 604.5p by 1000 GMT in a generally weak market. Lloyds TSB, which owns Cheltenham & Gloucester, was up 2p at 379.

Broker Panmure Gordon said it had reiterated its "buy" recommendation on Abbey. Banking analyst David Poutney said the recommendation was based partly on news that mortgage activity in August was 26 percent up on a year ago.
The results of an industry survey published in the Financial Times also found that confidence in the housing market is at its highest point this year.
The Barclays Mortgages Index, which tracks mortgage activity through UK solicitors, found that 49 percent of homeowners expected house prices to increase in the next 12 months.

"In addition, there's the withdrawal by Cheltenham & Gloucester of all their discounted mortgage offers apart from cash-backs on fixed rates," said Poutney, adding he saw 700p as a reasonable target price.
